claims.text: Bulk arc-melted or melt-spun non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type HEAs form an ordered single-phase hexagonal structure.
The bulk FeMnNiGeSi-type material undergoes a sharp, hysteretic first-order magnetostructural transition.
The low surface area of bulk ingots or melt-spun microribbons limits their heat-exchange rate.
Sputter deposition onto textured or porous substrates increases the alloy's surface-to-volume ratio relative to the stated bulk baseline.
Textured or porous substrates produce greater interfacial density and an altered grain or nucleation structure in the deposited films.
Greater interfacial density increases the density of heterogeneous nucleation sites during the first-order magnetostructural transition.
Additional heterogeneous nucleation sites distribute the transition over a wider temperature range.
Broadening the transition reduces its abruptness and associated hysteretic losses.
The broadened transition can retain a large magnetocaloric entropy change.
Films on textured or porous substrates will show a more gradual magnetostructural transition than the stated bulk baseline.
Films on textured or porous substrates will exhibit less hysteresis than the stated bulk baseline.
Films on textured or porous substrates will exhibit improved heat-exchange efficiency.
The proposed effects will occur during low-applied-field cycling near the magnetostructural transition temperature.
Processing conditions can affect phase stability, composition, and functional properties in HEAs.
Processing-induced changes in alloy homogeneity or microstructure can alter magnetocaloric behavior.
The magnitude of hysteresis reduction and heat-exchange improvement depends on the microstructure obtained through deposition.

contradictions.description: The material is called 'as-deposited' while the identified initial state and baseline are arc-melted ingots or melt-spun microribbons, which are not deposited films. The phrase 'as-deposited bulk baseline' therefore conflates distinct processing states.

The prediction is framed relative to a bulk ingot or microribbon baseline, but the falsification experiment compares textured/porous-substrate films with flat-substrate films. These different comparators do not directly test the stated bulk-relative prediction.
